---
title: "Linear regression"
format: live-html
pyodide:
  packages:
    - micropip
---

Compile and sample a small linear regression with [`pystanwasm`](https://github.com/habakan/pystanwasm),
via [Quarto Live](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/) -- interactive `{pyodide}` code blocks in an
ordinary Quarto document. Same bridge as the other demos.

Everything runs in a single block: Quarto Live tries to share Python state between separate `{pyodide}`
blocks on a page by serializing the global namespace between them, which breaks once that namespace holds
a live JS object reference (`pyodide.ffi.JsProxy`, unhashable/unpicklable) -- as `pystanwasm`'s bridge
does internally to cache the loaded wasm module. A single block sidesteps that entirely.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
import json
import micropip
from pyodide.code import run_js

# self.location.origin alone is wrong on a GitHub-Pages-style project site
# (https://host/repo-name/) -- it omits "/repo-name". self.location.href
# resolves to the *kernel worker's own* script URL, which does include it.
# Quarto Live's worker lives under a per-document "<name>_files/libs/
# quarto-contrib/" directory, so recovering the page's own directory needs
# trimming back to the slash before that, not just slicing at a marker.
site_base = run_js(
    """
    (() => {
      const href = self.location.href;
      const quarto = href.match(/^(.*)\\/[^\\/]+_files\\/libs\\/quarto-contrib\\//);
      if (quarto) return quarto[1];
      const markers = ["/extensions/", "/assets/"];
      for (const marker of markers) {
        const idx = href.indexOf(marker);
        if (idx !== -1) return href.slice(0, idx);
      }
      return self.location.origin;
    })()
    """
)

wheel_url = site_base + "/pystanwasm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
await micropip.install(wheel_url)

import numpy as np
import pystanwasm as stan

print("pystanwasm", stan.__version__)

stan_code = """
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] x;
  vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  y ~ normal(alpha + beta * x, sigma);
}
"""
data = {"N": 5, "x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "y": [2.1, 3.9, 6.2, 7.8, 10.1]}

model = stan.StanModel(stan_code, stanwasm_path="/stanwasm/pkg/stanwasm.js")
fit = await model.sampling(data=data, iter=2000, warmup=1000, seed=42)
print("parameters:", fit.param_names)

# fit.to_dataframe() is on the natural (constrained) scale -- sigma is
# already positive here, not log-scale.
beta = fit["beta"]
print(f"beta: mean={beta.mean():.3f} sd={beta.std():.3f}")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 4))
plt.hist(beta, bins=30)
plt.title("beta posterior")
plt.show()
```
